fcce94c088.q: Why do siloed identity and access management teams across workforce, Scion, and PAM domains prevent organizations from addressing non-human identity and AI agent authentication needs?
fcce94c088.a: Organizations operate with different teams working independently on workforce, Scion, and PAM, each with different tools that don't talk to each other. This siloed structure makes it difficult to escalate and move into the needs of new types of identities and new capabilities. Identity governance is primarily applied only to workforce, leaving other domains fragmented and unable to leverage shared learnings or unified approaches.
fcce94c088.e: One team, every identity: A PwC Leader on Breaking Down Identity Security Silos
fcce94c088.rq: If we don't integrate these two worlds, like identity and cyber, you will continue having breaches for forever.

f9aef32661.q: What problems occur when organizations try to apply traditional PAM and multi-factor authentication practices to non-human identity management?
f9aef32661.a: Traditionally PAM was about password management and session recording, but when organizations try to accommodate non-human identity within this traditional PAM program, it doesn't work. Applying multi-factor authentication to non-human identity is not feasible and doesn't make sense. Instead, organizations need to apply security using policies to block users or context-based authorization without requiring MFA or step-up processes designed for humans.

8a77e3babb.q: How does PwC's Zero Trust capability model integrate workforce, Scion, and non-human identity into a unified framework?
8a77e3babb.a: The Zero Trust capability model combines capabilities from multiple domains: workforce lifecycle management, Scion strong authentication and identity verification, non-human identity or security, and real-time policy evaluation during authentication flows. PwC creates agents representing specific personas, such as a manager doing certification campaigns every four months, to assess whether an organization has good zero-trust implementation, bad zero-trust, or no zero-trust, and identifies which capabilities should be applied.

9f76c8d881.q: Why is integrating cybersecurity and identity teams essential for preventing breaches, and what is the main barrier to achieving this integration?
9f76c8d881.a: If identity and cybersecurity teams don't integrate these two worlds, organizations will continue having breaches forever. Traditionally, identity and access management was completely separate from cybersecurity control and cybersecurity didn't look at identity as something really important. The solution requires embedding cybersecurity capability in the identity fabric and applying identity threat detection and response with real-time analysis and controls, not just having them on separate reporting lines.

5f6ba8201a.q: How does identity verification capability, originally built for consumer identity, now apply to workforce identity management in Europe?
5f6ba8201a.a: Identity verification is a capability that was built for consumer identity and client-facing systems, but now it is being used for workforce identity. In Europe, with the introduction of the EU identity wallet, workforce teams are adopting verification practices that were previously only applied in consumer-facing contexts, recognizing that workforce identity requires the same level of verification sophistication.
